entrances.note: In by the door from the Lane, at left.
In from the Lane, under the pole (errata 183).

LOOK_AT.say: A leather strop on a hook, polished to a mirror down the middle by ten thousand strokes.
repeat: Two straps, one canvas, one leather. Canvas first, then leather. He showed me, though I hadn't asked.
The leather is darker where his hand holds it. He has stood in exactly that place for years.

LISTEN_TO.say: It swings a little when the door goes, and slaps the chair once, like a reminder.
repeat: Slap, swing, still.
Nothing. The strop is between shaves, like the rest of us.

overrides.PULL: It pulls back. Strops do. I let go before it made a point of it.

LOOK_AT.say: A jar on the shelf, which I am not going to look in. I have decided.
repeat: I looked in the jar. I'd like to go back to not having looked in the jar.
The jar. I know what's in it now, and the jar knows I know.

LISTEN_TO.say: A faint clink from inside when the floor moves. I'm not going to think about what clinks.
repeat: Clink.
I'm not listening to the jar any more. The jar has had enough of my attention.

overrides.OPEN: No. I have looked in the jar. I am not going in the jar.

LOOK_AT.say: SHAVE 2 BITS. TOOTH 4 BITS. LIMB $1. The limb is the bargain, which worries me.
repeat: No price for a haircut. Either it's free, or he doesn't do them, and I'm afraid to find out which.
Someone has scratched a name under LIMB, and then scratched it out again. I hope he kept the limb.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. The prices speak for themselves, and loudly.
repeat: The board tapping against the wall in the draft: two bits, four bits, a dollar.
Nothing. It's said its prices. It doesn't haggle.

LOOK_AT.say: A mirror, with a crack running across it at about the height of a nervous man's chin.
repeat: Me, in a barber's mirror, looking like a man who needs a shave and is going to think about it first.
The crack goes right through my reflection's neck. I've decided not to read anything into it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. The mirror keeps its opinions on its face.
repeat: Nothing. It's turned to the wall a little, as if it had seen enough.
Nothing. Mirrors are the only thing in Consolation that never argue.

LOOK_AT.say: Instruments. I have identified the razor. I am choosing not to identify the others.
repeat: Laid out in a row from small to alarming. The razor is at the small end, which is the only comfort the tray offers.
Everything on it has been cleaned. I can tell, because it has been cleaned the way you clean something you've used.
Steel settling on cloth when I lean on the shelf.
Nothing. I've stepped back. That will do.

overrides.PICK_UP: I'd rather the instruments stayed with a man who knows which is which.

LOOK_AT.say: One chair, for shaves, teeth and limbs alike. The arms have straps.
repeat: There is a bucket beside it. The bucket is for the teeth, I hope.
It reclines with a lever. Every man who has sat in it has learned the word 'reclines' the hard way.
then: I'm told the straps are for the teeth.

LISTEN_TO.say: The leather creaking as it settles. It has heard every kind of language a man knows.
repeat: A spring, deep inside, sighing at the very idea of me.
Nothing. It's waiting with the patience of a thing that always gets its man.

PULL.say: The lever. It went flat at once, like a trap, and came up again slowly, like a trap being set. I have learned the word 'reclines' from the outside. I gather that is a first.
